description: Ticket has been scoped but work has not started yet.
Ticket is actively being worked on.
Ticket cannot proceed until an external dependency or decision is resolved.
Work is complete and closed — the same value also appears as a run's final_status when a run finishes successfully.
Epic-tier ticket has been scoped into child tickets; the epic itself has no direct implementation of its own.
Bug fix or minimal targeted change with self-evident intent — uses the short Scope to Implement to Test to Parity to Verify to Finalize pipeline.
New feature, refactor, or substantive repair — uses the full pipeline including Investigate/Plan/Review.
Large multi-ticket initiative that only scopes child tickets — no direct implementation happens on the epic ticket itself.
Highest priority — critical, blocking issue.
High priority — the default priority when unspecified.
Medium priority.
Low priority.
Fixes incorrect behavior.
Adds new capability.
Restructures existing code without changing its behavior.
Maintenance work with no direct feature or bug-fix impact.
Restores previously-working behavior that regressed.
Verify phase found one or more failing Definition-of-Done conditions.
Architecture or Security review found fixable violations that must be addressed before continuing.
Scope phase found this ticket duplicates or conflicts with existing work.
Plan phase raised unresolved questions that require a human decision before implementation can proceed.
Test phase found one or more failing tests.
Security review found a fundamental vulnerability that blocks the change.
The user interrupted or stopped the run before it reached a gate outcome.
A gate check failed — a generic/legacy status predating more specific gate-failure codes.
A batch of tickets were all successfully scoped (create-tickets workflow outcome).
Work completed successfully but was not associated with a specific ticket record.
Legacy alias of INPROGRESS from older monitoring records — same meaning: actively being worked on.
Duplicate or conflicting ticket found during Scope.
A tag used on this ticket is not registered in docs/guidelines/tag_registry.jsonl.
Some other Definition-of-Done condition failed at Verify — a deliberately coarse fallback covering any DoD failure not broken out into its own code.
Agent completed its task successfully.
Agent returned an error or could not complete its task.
Agent was blocked by a gate condition, such as an architecture violation.
This phase was skipped — for example Investigate/Plan/Review are skipped for hotfix-tier tickets.
Ticket-scoper agent creates the ticket file and staging artifacts, checking first for duplicate or conflicting work already underway.
Digs into the affected code, docs, and prior tickets for a ticket or proposed concern, producing the findings later phases build on.
Planner agent turns investigation findings into an ordered, narrow, independently-verifiable implementation plan with explicit scope guards.
Architecture-reviewer agent checks a proposed implementation plan against durable-state, API-boundary, and Mechanics Bible rules before any code is written.
Implementer agent writes the code changes described in the plan, or, in implement-epic, delegates one full implement-ticket run per child ticket.
Architecture-reviewer agent re-checks the real code diff after implementation, judging only findings flagged by its own static pre-check rather than re-reviewing the whole plan.
Test-scoper agent maps the changed files to relevant existing tests, runs a scoped test command, and reports pass/fail results.
Parity-updater agent updates the relevant docs/parity_ledger entry so documentation and source code stay in sync after a behavior change.
Security-reviewer agent checks changed code for injection, unsafe deserialization, secrets, and raw-domain-model exposure; runs only when the ticket is tagged security-relevant.
Confirms the work is genuinely complete against its own Definition-of-Done conditions - a 13-condition check in implement-ticket, or a regression/anchor-coverage check in simq-audit.
Moves the ticket to tickets/done/, appends the working log, migrates staging artifacts to storage, and cleans up any leftover run data.
Reads a natural-language proposal document and extracts its discrete concerns before any investigation begins.
Synthesis agent turns per-concern investigation results into properly-formed ticket fields, including real file paths and concrete acceptance criteria.
Writes the finished TCK-YYYYMMDD ticket file(s) into the target output folder.
Appends newly-created ticket IDs to a parent epic ticket's Related Tickets section, when an epic_id was given.
Re-runs the SimQ calibration corpus and captures regressions, pass/fail counts, and any uncovered anchor keys or parity ledger candidates.
Classifies each flagged calibration item as expected drift, a real regression, a design-acknowledgment decision, or no action needed.
Updates grade-anchor baselines for items classified as expected drift only, then re-runs a targeted test subset to confirm the update holds.
Updates the SimQ evaluation and integration docs so they stay consistent with the refreshed calibration results.
Updates docs/parity_ledger entries flagged by the SimQ audit gap scan, using the same verified/divergent/missing rules as implement-ticket's own Parity phase.
Reports the audit's final verdict, either suggesting a no-regression chore commit or handing off a pre-seeded ticket for a real regression or design-acknowledgment decision.
